topic: Mughal art and architecture — mixed tiers
description: Akbar to Aurangzeb monuments, painting schools, charbagh, pietra dura, jharokha

questions.stem: The Taj Mahal at Agra was commissioned by which Mughal emperor in memory of his wife?
questions.explanation: Taj Mahal — Shah Jahan, in memory of Arjumand Banu Begum (Mumtaz Mahal), who died 1631 (childbirth, 14th child). Construction 1632-1653 on the right bank of Yamuna at Agra. Chief architect — Ustad Ahmad Lahauri (also designed Red Fort). Material — white Makrana marble (Rajasthan); red sandstone for outer mosque + Mehmaan Khana. Pietra dura — semi-precious stones (jade, lapis, jasper) inlaid into marble. UNESCO 1983. Aurangzeb's wife Dilras Banu's tomb is the 'Bibi ka Maqbara' at Aurangabad ('poor man's Taj'), built by his son Azam Shah. Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb in Agra (Nur Jahan, for her father) — smaller, called 'Baby Taj', precursor to pietra dura.

questions.stem: The Buland Darwaza, the imposing 54-m gateway, is part of which complex built by Akbar to commemorate his Gujarat victory (1573)?
questions.explanation: Buland Darwaza ('high gateway', 54 m) — added 1576 by Akbar to the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri after his Gujarat victory. Fatehpur Sikri served as Akbar's capital 1571-1585; abandoned probably due to water shortage. Notable structures: Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas (with central pillar 'Akbar's throne'), Panch Mahal (5-storey wind tower), Jodha Bai's palace, Birbal's house, Salim Chishti's tomb (white marble, jali screens — earliest white-marble Mughal tomb). UNESCO 1986. Persian inscription on the Buland Darwaza: 'The world is a bridge, pass over it but build no houses on it' (Quranic). Akbar's syncretic Din-i-Ilahi (1582) was promulgated here.

questions.stem: Pietra dura (Italian for 'hard stone') — extensively used on the Taj Mahal — refers to:

options.option_text: Inlaying cut and polished semi-precious stones into marble to form decorative motifs

questions.explanation: Pietra dura — Italian, parchin kari in Persian. Cut + polished semi-precious stones (jasper, jade, lapis lazuli, carnelian, turquoise, malachite, mother-of-pearl) inlaid into marble or hard-stone. Reached its zenith on the Taj Mahal — floral motifs around the cenotaphs and dado panels. Earlier example — Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb (1622-28). Distinct from PIETRA TENERA (soft-stone) and from KASHIKARI (glazed tilework, used in Lahore Fort). The technique was likely brought from Italy via Mughal contacts but became a distinctive Mughal art form. Other notable techniques in Mughal architecture: jali (perforated stone screens), foliated arches, double dome (introduced at Humayun's Tomb).

questions.stem: The 'charbagh' garden layout, a hallmark of Mughal landscape design, is characterised by:

options.option_text: A garden divided into FOUR quadrants by water channels meeting at a central pool — symbolising the four rivers of Paradise

questions.explanation: Charbagh — Persian 'four gardens'. Layout: 4 quadrants divided by intersecting water channels (representing the 4 rivers of Paradise — water, milk, wine, honey — Quranic image). Introduced by Babur (Aram Bagh / Ram Bagh, Agra — earliest). Most famous examples: Humayun's Tomb (the first monumental charbagh tomb in India, ~1572); Taj Mahal (the tomb is offset to the rear edge instead of the centre — unusual); Shalimar Bagh (Kashmir, Jahangir 1619); Pinjore Gardens (Haryana, Aurangzeb's foster brother Fidai Khan). Water flows by gravity through chadar (cascade) and chini-khana (niche where lamps were placed behind falling water).

questions.stem: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi (1572) is historically significant primarily because it:

options.option_text: Introduced the Persian-style double dome and charbagh tomb to India — direct precursor to the Taj Mahal

questions.explanation: Humayun's Tomb — commissioned 1565 by Empress Bega Begum (Haji Begum, Humayun's senior widow) ~9 years after his death (he fell down the library stairs of Sher Mandal in Purana Qila in 1556). Architect — Mirak Mirza Ghiyas (Persian). Significance: (1) FIRST garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent (charbagh); (2) Introduced the double dome — outer is bulbous, inner is shallower; (3) Red sandstone with white marble accents → set the template for the Taj Mahal. UNESCO 1993. Last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar took refuge here in 1857 → captured by William Hodson.

questions.stem: Mughal painting reached its peak under JAHANGIR. Which feature distinguished his court atelier?

options.option_text: Bold colours; battle and hunt scenes were favoured (as under Akbar)
Refined naturalism — delicate portraits, detailed studies of birds, flowers, and animals (Ustad Mansur was the master nature-painter)

questions.explanation: Mughal-painting evolution: AKBAR — illustrations of manuscripts (Hamzanama, Akbarnama, Razmnama — Persian Mahabharata); large-scale, narrative; Persian-Indian fusion; Daswanth + Basawan were star painters. JAHANGIR — refined, naturalistic; courtly portraits; flora/fauna studies. USTAD MANSUR (his court painter) — known for the Siberian Crane and Dodo paintings. Abu'l Hasan was titled 'Nadir-uz-Zaman' (wonder of the age) for portraits. SHAH JAHAN — even more refined; Padshahnama; jeweled, formal. AURANGZEB — declined; he disapproved of figural art; many painters dispersed → seeded Rajput/Pahari schools (Kangra, Mewar, Bundi).

questions.stem: A 'jharokha' in Mughal architecture refers to:

options.option_text: A cantilevered enclosed balcony with stone brackets and jali, typically projecting from an upper-storey wall
A domed pavilion at a corner

questions.explanation: Jharokha — projecting balcony, often supported on stone brackets, with a small dome / chhatri above; often features jali (lattice) screens for purdah viewing. Used widely in Mughal + Rajput architecture (Hawa Mahal, Jaipur, has 953 jharokhas). Akbar instituted 'Jharokha Darshan' — appearing daily to subjects; abolished by Aurangzeb (Islamic puritan). Other elements to know: CHHATRI — domed pavilion / kiosk on roof or corners, signifies royalty; IWAN — vaulted recessed entrance hall; PISHTAQ — large rectangular frame of an iwan (the iconic frame of the Taj's main entrance); CHADAR — sloped water cascade in gardens.
